overview:
Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom completely surrounded by South Africa, one of only three countries in the world enclosed by a single neighbor. About the size of Maryland, it is the only nation on Earth that lies entirely above 1,000 meters, which is why it is called the Kingdom in the Sky. The capital, Maseru, sits on the western border along the Caledon River, and almost all the rest of the country is a tumble of high peaks, deep valleys, and grassy plateaus.

Around 2.3 million people live in Lesotho, and nearly all are Basotho, sharing one language, Sesotho, along with English as a second official tongue. Lesotho is a constitutional monarchy: the king is a symbol of the nation, while an elected parliament and prime minister run the government. It is a poor country where many people herd sheep and goats, grow corn, or work in South Africa's mines and factories. Lesotho sells water and electricity from its mountain dams to its giant neighbor, and its textile factories make jeans for American brands.
landAndNature: Lesotho's mountains are the Maloti and the Drakensberg, which rise to Thabana Ntlenyana at 3,482 meters, the highest point in southern Africa. Because of the altitude, winters are cold and snowy, unusual for Africa, and the country has a ski resort, Afriski. Rivers born here, including the Orange River, called the Senqu in Lesotho, cut spectacular gorges; Maletsunyane Falls drops 192 meters in a single plunge into a misty canyon. The Katse Dam, one of Africa's tallest, stores water sold to South Africa. The lowlands in the west are the only farmable strip. The rare bearded vulture nests on cliffs, and the spiral aloe, a plant whose leaves form a perfect spiral, grows only in these mountains. Dinosaur footprints are scattered in the sandstone.
peopleAndCulture: The Basotho are famous for their blankets: thick wool blankets in bold patterns are worn like cloaks by men and women against the mountain cold and given at weddings and coming-of-age ceremonies. The mokorotlo, a conical straw hat shaped like a mountain, is the national symbol and appears on the flag. Sure-footed Basotho ponies carry riders along mountain trails, and pony trekking is a national pastime. Most people are Christian. Meals center on papa, a stiff corn porridge, with moroho greens, beans, or meat, and sour porridge called motoho. Famo music, driven by the accordion, is played at gatherings, and lithoko praise poems honor chiefs and heroes. Soccer is the favorite sport, and Lesotho's long-distance runners compete internationally.
history: San hunter-gatherers painted rock shelters here thousands of years ago, and Sotho-speaking farmers arrived by the 1500s. In the early 1800s, as wars swept southern Africa, a chief named Moshoeshoe I gathered refugees onto the flat-topped mountain of Thaba Bosiu and united them into the Basotho nation, defeating attackers through clever diplomacy and defense. To protect his people from Boer settlers who took the fertile lowlands, Moshoeshoe asked Britain for protection in 1868, and Basutoland became a British protectorate. Independence came on October 4, 1966, as the Kingdom of Lesotho under King Moshoeshoe II. Decades of political disputes, a coup in 1986, and unrest in 1998 followed, but elections have continued, and the kingdom remains a distinct nation inside South Africa.
funFacts: Lesotho is the only country in the world whose entire territory lies more than 1,000 meters above sea level.
The Basotho blanket became a national dress after a British official gave one to King Moshoeshoe I in the 1860s.
Lesotho has one of the highest pubs in Africa, at the top of Sani Pass at 2,874 meters.
Fossilized footprints of dinosaurs are so common in Lesotho that some are used as landmarks by local herders.
The country is one of only three in the world enclosed entirely by a single neighbor, along with San Marino and Vatican City.
